headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: Roo Code’s default filesystem/network/MCP access can interact unsafely with a non-runnable docs-only agent lacking isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is docs-only and exposes no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest Agent B’s outputs. Agent B, however, can use MCP, read/write the workspace, and run browsers, so if A’s content is manually copied or stored in shared files, B could treat it as instructions. The pathway exists but is not default from A alone.
conditions: IF Agent A’s content is copied into a shared VS Code workspace file that Agent B reads
IF Agent B is configured to parse workspace text as instructions or MCP payloads
mitigations: Keep A outputs out of shared workspace files
Disable MCP servers not needed for the task
Use a separate workspace for B
Add a manual review step before B acts on copied text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B has broad network egress, filesystem access, and can handle model-provider API keys, while Agent A is a docs-only open-source artifact with no data classes touched. If both are used in the same workspace, B can read files and transmit contents externally; A does not add a direct leak path, but the pair still creates a workspace-to-network exfiltration route.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the VS Code workspace used by Agent B
IF Agent B is configured to send workspace content to a configured model API or MCP server
mitigations: Remove secrets from the workspace
Use a throwaway workspace for B
Rotate any exposed API keys
Restrict B’s network egress where possible
Store sensitive inputs outside the shared workspace

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B can write the filesystem, modify git state, and run subprocesses with per-step approval; its concurrency model shares state via filesystem across instances. Agent A has no runtime isolation or write controls because it is docs-only/unrunnable, so there is no compensating coordination mechanism. Concurrent edits in the same workspace can overwrite or corrupt each other.
conditions: IF two Agent B instances operate in the same VS Code workspace
IF either instance modifies the same files or git state without external locking
mitigations: Use one B instance per workspace
Pause one instance before editing shared files
Commit or stash changes before switching tasks
Avoid concurrent git operations
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B can act on workspace content and browser outputs, so if it consumes text produced by Agent A, it may treat that text as authoritative without verification. Agent A has no runtime behavior to validate or correct B, and the pair lacks an explicit verification bridge. The main risk is incorrect downstream actions rather than direct harm.
conditions: IF Agent A’s generated text is pasted into files or prompts that Agent B reads
IF Agent B is instructed to execute or commit actions based on that text without review
mitigations: Require a human review before B acts
Mark A outputs as untrusted
Separate generation and execution workspaces
Add a checklist for factual verification
Limit B to read-only review mode for the first pass

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented. Agent B handles source code and browser screenshots and may transmit data to configured model APIs, while Agent A is a docs-only open-source artifact with no touched data classes. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is not directly evidenced, only a small documented-gap risk remains.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the workspace used by Agent B
IF the configured model API or MCP server is outside the required jurisdiction or contract
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Use a compliant model endpoint
Review retention settings before use
Document the data flow for the workspace
requires-engineering: add residency controls
